thread.title: Close Update: Stocks Turn Defensive as Gaming Stocks Slump, Technical Resistance Blocks Upside

author: MT Newswires
title: Close Update: Stocks Turn Defensive as Gaming Stocks Slump, Technical Resistance Blocks Upside
text:
Shutterstock photo Wall Street's major averages closed lower on Wednesday when disappointing results from the gaming sector overshadowed bullish economic data and strength in healthcare stocks. The Nasdaq took the brunt o f earnings -fueled losses, while the S&P 500 ended a five-day winning streak with a modest loss.
Video gaming stocks were today's laggards after disappointing guidance from Electronic Arts ( EA ) and Take Two Interactive ( TTWO ) drove the entertainment sector down 2.6%. The damage to the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite was mitigated, however, by better-than-expected results from Snap ( SNAP ) and Apple ( AAPL ) supplier Skyworks ( SWKS ).
Earning were also reported by General Motors (GM), Disney (DIS) and 21st Century Fox (FOX, FOXA) as Q4 earnings season hits its stride.
Wall Street was slightly defensive into the open as President Donald Trump's State of the Union address left market participants with little direction while a significant miss on German factory orders (-1.6% vs +0.3% estimates) with lackluster results from Daimler weighed on Europe's major bourses lower.
Stocks perked up on GM's upbeat results, but ran into strong technical resistance at the S&P's 200-day moving average. Unable to pierce 2,742, the S&P reversed course, dragging the other major averages lower in sympathy.
Related markets were mixed as the lack of direction in stocks was reflected in anemic demand for safe havens. A disappointing auction for 10-year Treasury notes left the security unchanged even as the rest of the yield curve was slightly richer. Gold was lower, copper was higher and oil futures were higher after two days in the red.
On the economic front, the US trade deficit narrowed by 11.5% to $49.3 billion in November from a revised record high deficit of $55.7 billion, below the average estimate of -$54.0 billion.
Non-farm productivity increased by 1.3% last quarter but missed the estimated 1.6%. Additionally, Q3 productivity was revised down slightly to 2.2% from 2.3% originally.
